behavior_notes: A STALE CLAIM FIXED IN PASSING, and it is the same defect class one level down. Shape::WITNESS named DefEqBinder and described it as the deepest-per-level descent, i.e. the one that overflows first. The measurement contradicts that: defeq binder congruence uses two kernel frames per level and is nonetheless the CHEAPEST of the four, so it overflows LAST. The witness still fired, because Budget::DEFAULT on 2 MiB overflows on any shape -- which is exactly why nobody noticed. A witness that passes for a reason other than the one stated beside it is evidence that has stopped being true without anything going red. WITNESS is now the measured worst.

COST: twelve subprocess probes, no bisection, 0.18 seconds for the whole file including the four pre-existing guards. The stack is 4 MiB on purpose -- the prediction substitutes STACK_ENTRY_RESERVE_BYTES for the measured intercept, an error under 1% at that size and 4% at 1 MiB, which at 1 MiB would eat into the band.

IT BRACKETS RATHER THAN RE-DERIVES. The check never recomputes the constant and compares the result to itself, which would be the same number twice and would prove nothing. It asks the real descent questions whose answers are only all correct when the claim is true, and it takes the claim as a PARAMETER so the planted violations can hand it deliberately wrong numbers -- half the true cost, three times the true cost, and an entry reserve of 8 KiB -- and require a refusal naming the specific direction. A check that cannot fail is a rubber stamp.

THE DRIFT IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHESISED. Two observations on 2026-07-25, both on franken_lean-kxbj's row: the same instrument read 5,935.3 bytes/depth on the development host and 6,553.6 on an RCH remote worker at the identical (profile, arch, os); and widening Budget for franken_lean-4o3n cost two of the four shapes one level of ceiling. Neither was caught by anything. Both were caught because a human re-ran an ignored test on a hunch.

THE GUARDS THAT ALREADY EXISTED PROVE SURVIVAL AT THE SHIPPED PAIRING, which is a different claim from the shipped number still describing the descent. With STACK_SAFETY_FACTOR at 2 and MIN_STACK_BYTES rounded up on top of it there is roughly 3x of headroom in which MEASURED_STACK_BYTES_PER_DEPTH can be fiction and every test still passes -- and when the headroom finally runs out the guard does not fail, it aborts the test binary uncatchably. The tripwire turns the safety factor from a silent absorber of drift into a margin with a tripwire in it.

THE TOLERANCES ARE JUSTIFIED RATHER THAN PICKED. High 25%: that is 2.4x the largest host-to-host spread yet observed (10.4%), so ordinary machine variation cannot redden the tree, and it is half of STACK_SAFETY_FACTOR, so it fires with the whole margin still unspent. Low 33%, deliberately looser, because the directions differ in consequence -- an understated constant is the direction that aborts processes, while an overstated one is not a safety failure but silently shrinks depth_for_stack_bytes for every caller and manufactures typed non-answers that nobody can tell from real ones, which under franken_lean-4o3n is exactly what erodes a consensus seat.

THE TWO DIRECTIONS ARE QUANTIFIED DIFFERENTLY, and getting that wrong would have made this a flake generator rather than a guard. ABOVE the claim is a property of ANY shape -- one descent costing more than the constant says is enough to make MIN_STACK_BYTES promise too little. BELOW the claim is a property of ALL shapes at once, because the constant is the MAXIMUM over the four descents and a single cheap descent is not evidence that it is overstated. defeq_binder measures 4,507 bytes/depth against the shipped 5,935, which is 24% below it BY DESIGN; a per-shape low bound would have parked a permanent tripwire 9 points from a correct value, and the first person to see it fire would have widened the band rather than read it. Caught while reading the numbers back, before landing.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER: it re-checks the constant on the machine and profile the suite happens to run in, which is the configuration that matters (cargo test) and is not every configuration. It is a benchmark-class bound (D7) with a stated margin, not a theorem, and it does not make ExecConfig able to distinguish two hosts that share a triple -- franken_lean-4o3n's row argues against narrowing it, because that would make every budget Extrapolated the moment it crossed a machine.

COST: about 25 s for the one-time -Zbuild-std compile, then under 3 s for all four lanes warm -- four times cheaper than the Miri set, because TSAN instruments native code instead of interpreting it. Neither detector subsumes the other: Miri finds UB with no observable effect on this hardware (which is the class the fixed defect belonged to, since aligned 32-bit loads do not tear) and TSAN runs real threads, the real allocator, and the syscalls Miri refuses.

EVIDENCE-ARRAY CORRECTION, cc_2: the first version of this row carried eight behavior notes and EMPTY unit/boundary/error/mutation arrays, and I reported it as carrying real evidence. It did not — it was narrative with no citations, which is the defect class this manifest exists to prevent, in my own row. The citations are now present, and the hand-run ones say so in their own text so nobody reads them as a standing lane.

IT FAILS ON THE REAL DEFECT. With dec_ref's mode probe reverted to the plain ptr::read it had before 8cd1d3b, against the real crate on the pinned toolchain, TSAN reports two data races -- core::ptr::read::<i32> and core::sync::atomic::atomic_sub::<i32,i32> -- and the process exits 66. Restored, exit 0. The revert was made by hand, run, and reverted; git confirms crates/fln-unsafe-abi clean afterwards, and nothing of it is committed.

OPERATIONAL TRAP FOUND WHILE MEASURING, and it decides whether a lane is real: on the planted defect libtest prints 'test result: ok. 1 passed' and the process THEN exits 66, because TSAN reports at teardown. A lane that greps for 'test result: ok', or reads the last line, reports a clean run while a data race was detected and printed. The exit code is the only reliable signal. This is recorded in the guard document because a wiring that gets it wrong is a green rubber stamp.

PARTIAL: this row covers the DETECTOR half only. The CI lane that runs these commands is .github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/check.sh, both cod_2's surface, and is handed over on the bead rather than claimed here. The bead stays in progress.

THE RUNNABLE LANE NOW EXISTS AS A SCRIPT; what remains is only its registration, which is cod_2 surface (.github/workflows/ci.yml and scripts/check.sh). The hard half -- getting TSAN to build at the pin, the exit-code semantics, the isolated target directory, and proving each lane actually ran -- is done and measured. Registration is two lines.

THE TWO DETECTORS NAME THE SAME RACE FROM OPPOSITE ENDS -- Miri says non-atomic read versus atomic read-modify-write and points at rc.rs; TSAN points at the core primitives each side bottoms out in. That agreement is worth something precisely because neither was derived from the other, which is the same argument as B3's two engines one layer down.

TSAN IS REACHABLE AT THE PIN, and the earlier claim that it was not was wrong for the same reason the earlier claim about Miri was wrong: nobody had installed rust-src for the pinned nightly and tried. -Zbuild-std rebuilds std under the same -Zsanitizer=thread, which removes the ABI-mismatch refusal that made it look impossible. Verified instrumented rather than assumed: 444 __tsan symbols in the test binary, including __tsan_func_entry and __tsan_atomic, and libstd rebuilt under the same flags.

The executed-check discriminates, observed rather than asserted: its first version compared the cargo FILTER against the printed test name, and `concurrent_publication` is a prefix of `concurrent_publication_of_one_target_never_yields_a_mixture`, so a lane that ran correctly was reported ran=no. Fixed to require the exact name, and the episode is recorded in the script because a guard that cannot tell "did not run" from "I do not recognise that name" is one that gets widened the first time it fires.

The guard reports THREE outcomes, not two: 0 pass, 1 a detector finding or a lane that did not run, 2 setup could not be established. Separated because "we could not look" is not "we looked and found nothing" (FL-INV-07), and a missing component must not read as a clean run.

The lanes must use an isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR: -Zsanitizer=thread invalidates every artifact built without it, so sharing the workspace target directory would force a full rebuild for the next pane and another when they rebuild without it.

behavior_notes: Also cc_3's, and not claimed here: the census today conflates 'ran out' with 'could not establish comparability' inside unscorable. The conservation law it asks for is decoded == compared + unscorable + incomparable, because an incomparability that is silent looks exactly like a clean run.

Cross-crate fallout was mechanical: Budget lost its struct-literal form, so three sites in crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs and one in crates/fln-verdict/src/reflection.rs became budget.narrowed(steps, depth). Same numbers, same semantics, no test intent changed.

On any target other than x86_64-linux the shipped measurement is Grade::Extrapolated, so no cross-engine comparison can be established there at all. A platform-matrix run would report zero disagreements, and zero disagreements would be the wrong thing to conclude.

Parity here is parity of the DERIVATION, never of the number. A bound detached from the configuration it was measured in is a number; attached to it, it is a measurement. Every claim in this row rests on the second, and on nothing the first would support.

THIS DOES NOT EARN AGREEMENT BETWEEN TWO ENGINES. There is no second engine: no NbE anywhere in the workspace, and fln-checker is an independence boundary and a data schema, not an implementation that decides verdicts. Fuel parity today is a property of ONE engine against its own execution configuration. A reader who takes 'fuel parity, tested' to mean the engines have been compared would be wrong, and that is the sentence most likely to be dropped when this row is summarised.

The measured dev/release gap is the evidence, not an illustration: 5,935 bytes of native stack per unit of depth in dev against 640 in release, for the identical depth 4096, same code and same target (bead franken_lean-kxbj). That is why an agreed depth NUMBER certifies nothing.

cc_3 -- paired on this bead, and the pane whose objection it is named for -- reviewed the shape before the commit. It withdrew its own Budget::planted() counter-proposal in favour of narrowed(), on the ground that there must be exactly one way to make a budget. It also named what these tests do NOT reach: comparability is necessary and not sufficient, because two established, honestly-measured, same-configuration bounds can still produce a comparison in which one run was truncated, and a comparison over a truncated run certifies nothing however well provenanced the truncation was. That margin half -- (allowed, observed) on both axes per compared declaration -- is cc_3's next build and is not claimed here.

cfg!(debug_assertions) is a PROXY for 'unoptimised' and verdict.rs names it as one, including its unsafe direction: a profile with debug assertions off and optimisation off is classed Release and handed a ceiling 9.3x too deep for its frames. The root Cargo.toml carries no profile overrides today, so that state is unreachable by accident rather than by construction; turning it into a refused state is cc_3's.

All-collision keys are CONSTRUCTED analytically, not searched: Lean mix_hash is invertible in its component argument, so k2 = f_inverse(f(k1) ^ h1 ^ h2) collides by construction. 24 distinct identities on one key hash.
Consequence: an adversary can force full-hash collisions on module identities with no search, which is why fln-amv.13's collision budget exists.

PMap admission work is Uncharged (registration uses the unbudgeted insert, so no fln-amv.13 facts are produced to hand off); decoder work is OwnedElsewhere{fln-20n.1}, enforced structurally because no UsageUnit denominates it.
Payload bytes is NOT swept at its boundaries: no fixture in this suite carries artifact payload bytes.

ReservationClaim is Unsupported with its reason: every allocating path in a publication is infallible-or-abort, so a reservation cannot be made genuine at this layer and is reported rather than implied.
The reduced-width overflow test is a MODEL of the checked-accumulate discipline; it does not compute the wide u128 counters.
A resource stop is typed Inconclusive and carries no clean-input diagnostic; trivia and raw-string boundaries are tested separately from token-table totality.

FOURTH INSTANCE of the discrimination-failure family, found by the audit this bead asked for. identity_digest fed format!("{:?}") - a Debug RENDERING - into the digest preimage at three sites (Sort's level, Const's level list, the FVar/MVar ids). bf9ef450 fixed the NAME half of this very function and left the level and id halves on Debug, with Canonical for Level already reachable in fln-hash and already used one line away. GENERALISATION ADDED: the serialisation rule recorded on 41s asks 'can two different values produce the same bytes?' and returns NO here, so it would have passed this file. The follow-up question this instance adds is 'is this projection a CONTRACT, or a rendering that happens to be injective today?' A renderer that discriminates by luck is a defect awaiting a refactor, and no collision test can see it.

LATENT, NOT ACTIVE, and deliberately not inflated: Level's Debug is a hand-written stack-safe copy of the DERIVED rendering and Name's Debug is structural, so no two distinct levels collide under it today. Checked, not assumed. Nothing was broken and no digest was wrong.

SCOPE NOTE: fixing intern.rs was not in this bead's title. It is here because the audit this bead asked for is what found it, the fix is eight lines in a file with zero production consumers, and filing it would have cost three governed artifacts to track work smaller than the bead describing it.

THE TEST IS WRITTEN AGAINST THE ENCODER, NOT AGAINST DISCRIMINATION, because Debug does discriminate today: a discrimination test would pass identically before and after the fix, prove nothing, and quietly certify the defect. The test independently recomputes the preimage and requires identity_digest to agree. KILLED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: reverting the Sort site to format!("{level:?}") fails it, verified by doing exactly that and restoring.

The amendment was applied to oh1j's description as a single VERIFIED substitution: reversing the replacement byte-reproduces the original, and the write-back was read back and compared. No other character of a 3261-character field moved.

WHAT WAS WRONG was that correctness rested on an accident nothing pinned, inside a function whose whole subject is identity. Level's own doc says its Debug is byte-identical to the derived rendering, so a field added or reordered in Level or its Node silently moves every digest preimage while every test stays green - the digest is a bucket hint confirmed by full Expr equality. The rendering also included Level's packed data word, a CACHED hash seed and depth, so the identity preimage depended on a cache rather than on structure.

A LIMIT OF THE CONFIGURATION MODEL, found by re-measuring on two machines: the same instrument at the same (profile, arch, os) measured 5,935 bytes/depth on this host and 6,553.6 on an RCH remote worker, a 10.4% spread that ExecConfig cannot distinguish. Grade::Measured is therefore a claim about a configuration CLASS, not about a host. It is safe -- 6,553.6 x 4096 = 26.8 MiB actual against 46.4 MiB budgeted -- and this is the first time the 2x safety factor has been asked to do anything. Narrowing ExecConfig to a host identity would make every budget Extrapolated the moment it crossed a machine, which is worse than the margin it would buy.

A depth ceiling above the stack it runs on is not a bound, it is a bound-shaped comment. A native stack overflow aborts the process uncatchably, so FL-INV-07 cannot be satisfied after the fact by catching anything; the guarantee is structural or it does not exist. It is now structural: the ceiling-below-floor relation is a const assertion checked when the kernel compiles, not a test that has to be remembered.

CORPUS RERUN, the last acceptance clause, discharged at HEAD against the pinned Reference: all 2,433 modules, zero stack overflows, terminal summary reached, and Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt at index 412 is byte-identical to cod_3's pre-existing v8 census INCLUDING its stream_digest -- decoded=65, compared=61, disagreements=0, unscorable=4, subject_no_answer=4, with typed Depth for instCommRingInt16/Int64/Int32 and Steps for Int8. The worker stack is now Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES, the kernel's own derived requirement, rather than a number picked to make a crash stop, so the clause about not using an unmeasured workaround is met in substance and not only in outcome.

RE-MEASURED at HEAD after franken_lean-4o3n widened Budget from 16 bytes to about 144: the slope is unchanged at 5,935.3 against a shipped 5,935. What moved is small and is recorded rather than fixed -- forall_infer and lam_infer each lost ONE level at both probe stacks while app_infer kept its, and the fitted intercept for those two rose by exactly one slope quantum, which is the coarsest unit a whole-depth bisection can report. So the true growth in fixed entry cost is in (0, 5935] bytes and this instrument cannot resolve it further. Cost: one unit of ceiling in 4,096, 0.02%, against a 64 KiB entry reserve that remains 2.4x the largest measured intercept.

THE LANE STILL EXITS 101, and not for this bead. It panics on fln-lst4's coverage clause -- kernel differential coverage silently stopped: 156972 < 157183 scoreable declarations -- with numbers identical to cod_3's v8, so nothing here regressed it and nothing here fixes it. That clause is cod_3's lane. A red lane exit is not evidence against this bead and is not claimed as evidence for it.

The number is measured, not chosen: 5,935 bytes of native stack per unit of depth, dev profile, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, taken black-box by bisecting the deepest surviving descent at two known stack sizes in a subprocess so the fixed entry cost solves out of the slope. depth stays 4,096 deliberately -- that is a POLICY choice about checking power, and the thing that was uncalibrated was the stack it silently assumed, so relocating 4,096 would have moved an uncalibrated bound rather than calibrating one.

The witness asserts the FAILURE as well as the fix: Budget::DEFAULT on a 2 MiB thread -- the exact pairing that killed the Tribunal on this module -- must STILL abort inside a contained subprocess, and the same run under Budget::for_stack_bytes(2 MiB) must not. If that test ever stops dying, the hazard has moved and the calibration is measuring the wrong thing. A silently-passing calibration is worse than no calibration.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER: a benchmark-class claim (D7) over four SYNTHETIC descents on one target at one optimisation level. It is not a proof that no corpus term is worse than forall_infer, and the 2x factor is a margin rather than a theorem. The strongest available follow-up is to run the real Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt declarations through the same probe at varying stack sizes and confirm they sit under the synthetic worst; that needs the olean decode path and belongs to the conformance lane.

A BUILD-GATE IS THE ONLY AVAILABLE MECHANISM HERE, not the second-best one. fln-env is rank 4 and fln-kernel rank 6, so an fln-env -> fln-kernel edge is rejected by this same guard and fln-env can never name a kernel-bound capability type. Sealing a trait excludes fln-kernel by the definition of sealing; an unsealed trait excludes nobody; a token minted by fln-env proves nothing about its holder; a Cargo feature is additive and global so any dependent re-opens the hole for the whole graph. A type-level guarantee needs a plan amendment to section 5 layering.
